title: The Singh Families Are Removed and Binjhu Declares War

blocks.text: Once the harassment becomes intolerable, the Singhs start pulling their families out of Brar households and placing them in safer settlements such as village Guru-ke-Kothay. The move makes clear that the conflict is no longer a matter of insults alone; both communities are preparing for sustained hostility.

From there the dispute escalates into open organization for war, and the Brars of Binjhu declared war rather than stepping back from the provocation. Armed bands gather, attacks become regular, and the countryside begins to take on the feel of a local campaign rather than a village quarrel.

The page closes by setting up an armed encounter between the Singhs and the Brars, with the Brars leaning on spear warfare while the Singhs answer with tighter discipline and firearms. The relocation of families and the call to arms together mark the true opening of the Brar conflict.
